titleStmt.title: Stress facilitates classical conditioning in males, but impairs classical conditioning in females through activational effects of ovarian hormones
titleStmt.author: Gwendolyn E. Wood
Tracey J. Shors

publicationStmt.p: Tag layer of the DHSS Meta-Tagging Project. The article text is reproduced from the staged copy named in sourceDesc and is not altered; the tags are held separately in standOff so that overlapping and nested spans are preserved.

bibl.title: Stress facilitates classical conditioning in males, but impairs classical conditioning in females through activational effects of ovarian hormones
bibl.publisher: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: the effect of an acute stressor on acquisition of the classically conditioned eyeblink response in male and female rats, and the role of ovarian hormones in the female effect
span.quote: we investigated sexually dimorphic effects of a stressor of restraint and intermittent tailshock on classical eyeblink conditioning 24 h after stressor cessation

span.label: does stress enhance classical eyeblink conditioning in females as it does in males
span.quote: Based on these differences in learning and the apparent lack of stress-induced helplessness symptomatology in females, we tested whether stress would enhance classical eyeblink conditioning in females, as it does in males ( 10 – 13 ).

span.label: shows that the same stressor has opposite effects on associative learning in males and females, and that the female impairment requires ovarian hormones and available estrogen receptors
span.quote: In summary, these results indicate that exposure to the same aversive event can induce opposite behavioral responses in males vs. females.

span.label: mechanism
span.quote: We further demonstrate that the stress-induced impairment in female conditioning is dependent on the presence of ovarian hormones.

span.label: sexually dimorphic stress effects on classical eyeblink conditioning
span.quote: Based on evidence of sex differences in learning and responses to stressful events, we investigated sexually dimorphic effects of a stressor of restraint and intermittent tailshock on classical eyeblink conditioning 24 h after stressor cessation.

span.label: behavioural-experiment
span.quote: Male and female, stressed and unstressed rats were presented with paired ( n = 7) or explicitly unpaired ( n = 4) conditioning stimuli.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Stress impairs female conditioning by acting through circulating estrogen binding to available estrogen receptors, so removing either the hormone or the receptor blocks the impairment
span.quote: In combination with the ovariectomy results, these data suggest that the stress-induced impairment of classical conditioning in females is dependent on the presence of estrogen and the availability of estrogen receptors.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Stress disrupts ovarian hormone levels, and that disruption in turn impairs learning
span.quote: The stress-induced impairment of learning in females may be mediated by a stress-induced disruption of ovarian hormones.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Stress raises glucocorticoids through a sexually dimorphic hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal response, and the glucocorticoid rise disrupts estrogen and progesterone
span.quote: A disruption of estrogen and progesterone could be mediated by a rise in other stress-induced hormones, such as glucocorticoids.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Estrogen changes intracellular calcium through L-type calcium channels and NMDA receptor activation, altering synaptic density and efficacy and thereby the rate of learning
span.quote: Thus, changes in intracellular calcium via calcium channels or NMDA receptor activation are likely contributors to the effects of estrogen on synaptic density and efficacy, as well as the stress effects on learning reported here ( 12 ).

span.label: the paper's premise is a stated absence: the experiment exists because the question had never been asked of females
span.quote: To our knowledge, the effects of stress on classical conditioning have not been examined in females.

span.label: the ceiling explanation is not argued away but engineered away: the CS intensity is lowered until unstressed females start where unstressed males started, and the impairment survives
span.quote: To evaluate this explanation for the sexually opposed effects of stress on classical conditioning, we reduced the initial rate of acquisition in the unstressed females by decreasing the intensity of the CS ( 38 ).

span.label: two independent routes to the same conclusion: take out the organ that makes the hormone, then leave the organ and block the receptor instead
span.quote: In combination with the ovariectomy results, these data suggest that the stress-induced impairment of classical conditioning in females is dependent on the presence of estrogen and the availability of estrogen receptors.

span.label: the two converging routes do not agree in every detail, and the paper reports the disagreement rather than resolving it by preference
span.quote: These results suggest that removal of estrogen hormone and blockade of its receptor do not necessarily have similar consequences on learning and may activate different cellular processes.

span.label: a ladder of nonspecific explanations is eliminated one at a time with its own control — pseudoconditioning, sensitization, spontaneous blinking, first-trial responding, analgesia and motor activity
span.quote: Therefore, the sexually opposed effects of stress on acquisition of the CR was not attributable to nonspecific effects of stressor exposure on spontaneous blinking, sensitization, or pseudoconditioning.

span.label: the first trial is used as a control on the manipulation itself: if the stressor made animals respond to the tone directly, it would show before any learning was possible
span.quote: In addition, exposure to the stressor did not elicit responses to the CS on the first trial of training [Cochran Q test ( 3 ) = 0.82; P = 0.85], before any learning could have occurred.

span.label: the reflex itself is used as an argument that motor differences cannot explain the result, since every animal must produce the unconditioned response
span.quote: Moreover, changes in gross motor activity should not alter the ability to acquire the conditioned eyeblink response, and all rats must elicit the unconditioned eyeblink response to eyelid stimulation as part of a reflex.

span.label: the hormonal state is read out independently of the manipulation, by vaginal cytology, so the antagonist's effect can be confirmed rather than assumed
span.quote: The vaginal smears of females administered TAM (20 of 21) contained leukocytes and scattered epithelial cells, a cytology indicative of diestrus and low levels of estrogen.

span.label: a continuous cycle is collapsed into three stages by the authors, chosen to correspond to circulating hormone levels rather than to the underlying cytological detail
span.quote: We used a simplified three-stage classification scheme in which proestrus (early and mid proestrus), estrus (late proestrus and estrus), and diestrus (brief metestrus and diestrus combined) corresponded to basic differences in circulating hormone levels.

span.label: a transient effect and a persistent one are separated by looking at where each has gone by the end of training: the baseline sex difference washes out, the stress effect does not
span.quote: These results suggest that the differential performance between unstressed males and unstressed females can be overcome with continued training, while the dimorphic effects of stress on classical eyeblink conditioning are more persistent.

span.label: an unexpected reversal is reported rather than buried: ovariectomised females responded MORE after stress, putting them on the male side of the effect
span.quote: In fact, during the last 100 trials, OVX females exposed to the stressor responded more than the unstressed OVX females [ F (2, 68) = 3.34; P = 0.04], suggesting that the performance of OVX females can be facilitated in response to the stressor

span.label: Sex and stress each independently affect performance in learning tasks, which complicates attributing the observed differences to learning.
span.note: what this limits: any attribution of the effect to sex or to stress singly: EVALUATING THE CONTRIBUTION OF SEX AND STRESS TO LEARNING IS COMPLICATED BY THE FACT THAT BOTH VARIABLES ALTER PERFORMANCE IN LEARNING TASKS
span.quote: Evaluating the contribution of sex and stress to learning is complicated by the fact that both variables alter performance in learning tasks.

span.label: The ovariectomy result may reflect progesterone rather than estrogen, since removal of the hormone and blockade of its receptor gave different outcomes.
span.note: what this limits: the estrogen interpretation of the ovariectomy result: THE RESULTS MAY SUGGEST A CRITICAL ROLE FOR PROGESTERONE IN THE IMPAIRED PERFORMANCE ASSOCIATED WITH OVARIECTOMY
span.quote: Alternatively, the results may suggest a critical role for progesterone in the impaired performance associated with ovariectomy.

span.label: Hormone removal and receptor blockade did not have equivalent consequences for learning, so the cellular route of the effect is unresolved.
span.note: what this limits: any inference that treats hormone removal and receptor blockade as the same evidence: REMOVAL OF ESTROGEN HORMONE AND BLOCKADE OF ITS RECEPTOR DO NOT NECESSARILY HAVE SIMILAR CONSEQUENCES ON LEARNING AND MAY ACTIVATE DIFFERENT CELLULAR PROCESSES
span.quote: These results suggest that removal of estrogen hormone and blockade of its receptor do not necessarily have similar consequences on learning and may activate different cellular processes.

span.label: the two hormones cannot be separated by ovariectomy, which removes both estrogen and progesterone
span.note: what this limits: the same scope as item 1 - ovariectomy removes estrogen and progesterone together, so the two hormones cannot be separated by it
span.quote: Alternatively, the results may suggest a critical role for progesterone in the impaired performance associated with ovariectomy.

span.label: the antagonist is not clean at the receptor-subtype level
span.note: what this limits: the receptor-specificity of the pharmacological result: ESTROGEN HAS AT LEAST TWO TYPES OF NUCLEAR RECEPTORS ... AND TAM HAS BINDING AFFINITY FOR BOTH TYPES OF RECEPTORS TO VARYING DEGREES
span.quote: Estrogen has at least two types of nuclear receptors (α and β receptors) ( 40 ), and TAM has binding affinity for both types of receptors to varying degrees ( 45 ).

span.label: the estrous stage was not controlled in the main experiments, so the effect may be carried by one phase of the cycle
span.note: what this limits: the main stress effect, which may be carried by one phase of the cycle: THE EFFECTS OF STRESS ON ACQUISITION OF THE CR [may be] MEDIATED BY THE STAGE OF ESTROUS AND LEVELS OF CIRCULATING ESTROGEN
span.quote: These results raise the possibility that the effects of stress on acquisition of the CR are mediated by the stage of estrous and levels of circulating estrogen.

span.label: ovariectomy itself was not inert — it raised sensitized responding, and the paper has to argue that the increase is too small to matter
span.note: what this limits: the sensitization comparison specifically: OVARIECTOMY ALONE ENHANCED THE NUMBER OF SENSITIZED RESPONSES ... [called] THIS MINOR INCREASE - the surgery moved the baseline it was meant to hold still
span.quote: Ovariectomy alone enhanced the number of sensitized responses from <1 of 10, to 2 of 10 responses to a white noise stimulus alone [ F (1, 34) = 5.96; P < 0.05]. This minor increase in sensitized responses cannot account for the finding that OVX prevented the stress-induced impairment of CRs.

span.label: sex and stress are entangled as explanatory variables because each alters performance on its own
span.note: duplicate of: limitations[0] · what this limits: the same scope as item 0 - sex and stress are entangled because each alters performance on its own
span.quote: Evaluating the contribution of sex and stress to learning is complicated by the fact that both variables alter performance in learning tasks.

span.label: the mechanism linking stress to the hormones is proposed, not shown
span.note: what this limits: the mechanistic account only: THE STRESS-INDUCED IMPAIRMENT OF LEARNING IN FEMALES MAY BE MEDIATED BY A STRESS-INDUCED DISRUPTION OF OVARIAN HORMONES - proposed, not shown
span.quote: The stress-induced impairment of learning in females may be mediated by a stress-induced disruption of ovarian hormones.

span.label: vaginal smear staging, imported as an independent readout of hormonal state so that a behavioural manipulation can be checked against circulating estrogen
span.quote: For the TAM study, vaginal cytology was obtained through daily vaginal smears (12:00 to 14:00).

span.label: tamoxifen, a clinical antiestrogen, repurposed as a laboratory tool for asking whether a behaviour requires estrogen receptors
span.quote: Based on its antiestrogenic properties, TAM has been used as a tool to evaluate the role of estrogen in sexually dimorphic behaviors such as anxiety ( 47 ), agonistic behavior (e.g., ref. 48 ), and sexual receptivity (e.g., ref. 49 ).

span.label: sham surgery reproducing every part of the ovariectomy except the removal itself
span.note: eliminates: the surgery, anaesthesia and handling as the cause of any difference attributed to loss of the ovaries - the single difference is named in the sentence
span.quote: Sham surgery included all aspects of the OVX procedure, except the fallopian tube and ovaries were left intact.

span.label: measurements of spontaneous blinking, sensitization and pseudoconditioning alongside the conditioning result
span.note: eliminates: three alternatives at once - nonspecific effects of stressor exposure on blinking, sensitization, and pseudoconditioning · outcome: held
span.quote: Therefore, the sexually opposed effects of stress on acquisition of the CR was not attributable to nonspecific effects of stressor exposure on spontaneous blinking, sensitization, or pseudoconditioning.

span.label: comparison of analgesia following tailshock between males and females
span.note: eliminates: a sex difference in stress-induced analgesia as the reason the conditioning effects run in opposite directions
span.quote: These results suggest that the diametrically opposed effects of stress on classical conditioning in males vs. females are not attributable to gross differences in analgesia induced by previous exposure to the tailshock stressor.

span.label: conditioning — classical versus operant/instrumental; stress moves them in opposite directions, which is the dissociation the paper is built on
span.quote: In contrast to these effects on instrumental conditioning, exposure to a stressful event facilitates classical conditioning in males.

span.label: eyeblink — conditioned response (at least 80 ms after CS onset, before US onset) versus sensitized response (within 80 ms of CS onset); the same movement counted as two different things by latency
span.quote: Conditioned responses (CRs) occurred at least 80 ms after CS onset but prior to US onset on paired trials, or throughout the trial on CS alone trials. Eyeblinks that occurred within 80 ms of CS onset were considered sensitized responses.

span.label: impairment — as a stress effect within females, versus as an ovariectomy effect in unstressed females; the paper finds both and keeps them apart
span.quote: The loss of ovarian hormones also resulted in a learning impairment among unstressed females during late acquisition (last 100 out of 300 trials).

span.label: removing estrogen — by taking out the source (ovariectomy) versus by blocking the receptor (tamoxifen); the paper shows these are not equivalent operations
span.quote: It is noted that acquisition of the CR was impaired in OVX females, but the learning rate of females administered TAM was not significantly altered.

span.label: sex difference — the baseline one (unstressed females learn faster, and it washes out with training) versus the stress-induced one (opposite signs, and it persists)
span.quote: However, the sex difference in the rate of acquisition in unstressed rats was not as long-lasting as the stress effect.

span.label: estrous stage — the full cytological sequence versus the simplified three-stage scheme the authors impose to track circulating hormone levels
span.quote: Early proestrus is marked by pink staining epithelial cells, late proestrus and estrus by masses of dark blue staining cornified cells, and diestrus by dark staining leukocytes with scattered epithelial cells.

span.label: hormone effects — activational, depending on what circulates in the adult, as against the organisational sense implied by the title's contrast
span.quote: Overall, these results indicate that the stress-induced impairment of classical eyeblink conditioning in females is dependent on the activational effects of ovarian hormones.

span.label: claim_type: existence
span.note: a second reading DIFFERING from the recorded value. Recorded: mechanism — a second reading, verbatim-verified, disagreeing with the value on the record. Not applied - a person decides.
span.quote: Our results indicate that exposure to the acute stressor had diametrically opposed effects on the rate of acquisition of the conditioned response in male vs. female rats.

span.label: method: classical eyeblink conditioning in rats with implanted periorbital electrodes, 24 h after restraint-and-tailshock stress, crossed with ovariectomy and with estrogen-receptor blockade
span.note: a second reading DIFFERING from the recorded value. Recorded: behavioural-experiment — a second reading, verbatim-verified, disagreeing with the value on the record. Not applied - a person decides.
span.quote: A delay paradigm was used in which an 85-dB, 240-ms white noise CS with a 5-ms rise/fall time overlapped and coterminated with a 0.7-mA, 80-ms periorbital shock unconditioned stimulus (US).

span.label: phenomenon: sexually dimorphic effects of stress on associative learning
span.note: a second reading DIFFERING from the recorded value. Recorded: sexually dimorphic stress effects on classical eyeblink conditioning — a second reading, verbatim-verified, disagreeing with the value on the record. Not applied - a person decides.
span.quote: These effects underscore sex differences in associative learning and emotional responding, and implicate estrogen in the underlying neuronal mechanism.

span.label: extends → the male-only literature on stress-induced facilitation of classical conditioning (refs 10–15), by asking the same question of females for the first time
span.quote: To our knowledge, the effects of stress on classical conditioning have not been examined in females.

span.label: extends → reports that stress-induced helplessness is reduced or absent in females (refs 6–9)
span.quote: Interestingly, the performance deficit in response to a stressful event is reported to be significantly reduced, if not absent, in females ( 6 – 9 ).

span.label: contradicts → the expectation, stated as the paper's own hypothesis, that stress would enhance conditioning in females as it does in males
span.quote: Based on these differences in learning and the apparent lack of stress-induced helplessness symptomatology in females, we tested whether stress would enhance classical eyeblink conditioning in females, as it does in males ( 10 – 13 ).

span.label: supports → the body of evidence implicating estrogen in memory formation, including clinical work on estrogen and Alzheimer's
span.quote: Our data suggest that estrogen mediates the stress-induced impairment of associative learning, and adds to the growing body of evidence implicating a functional role for estrogen in effective memory formation.

span.label: supports → a later study establishing that the female impairment occurs preferentially in proestrus
span.quote: Indeed, a study subsequent to those presented here established that the stress-induced impairment of classical conditioning in females occurs preferentially in proestrus, when estrogen levels are high ( 50 ).

span.label: critiques → an activity-difference explanation of sex effects in learning tasks
span.quote: The findings presented here do not appear to be attributable to basic differences in activity.

span.label: classical conditioning —contrasted-with→ instrumental conditioning
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.95
span.quote: In contrast to these effects on instrumental conditioning, exposure to a stressful event facilitates classical conditioning in males.

span.label: learned helplessness —operationalised-as→ operant conditioning
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.85
span.quote: The impairment is typically observed during an operant conditioning task, in which an animal must perform an overt response to learn the operant contingency.

span.label: estrogen —part-of→ ovarian hormones
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.95
span.quote: Female sex hormones, estrogen and progesterone, are produced by the ovaries and influence learning and physiological responses to stress ( 22 , 23 ).

span.label: tamoxifen —causes→ estrogen receptors
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.95
span.quote: TAM binds reversibly to the estrogen receptor ( 39 ), and inhibits binding of tritiated estradiol ( 44 ).

span.label: conditioned eyeblink response —distinct-from→ sensitized responses
span.note: strength of the relation: 1
span.quote: Conditioned responses (CRs) occurred at least 80 ms after CS onset but prior to US onset on paired trials, or throughout the trial on CS alone trials. Eyeblinks that occurred within 80 ms of CS onset were considered sensitized responses.

span.label: estrous cycle —operationalised-as→ vaginal cytology
span.note: strength of the relation: 1
span.quote: The stages of the estrous cycle are reflected in the vaginal cytology.

span.label: RETRACTED (RE-GROUNDED) · estrogen —operationalised-as→ estrous cycle
span.note: RETRACTED: RE-GROUNDED. The old span listed cycle stages without naming the cycle. This sentence names both and ties them - 'the vaginal cytology of diestrus, A STAGE OF THE ESTROUS CYCLE ASSOCIATED WITH LOW ESTROGEN LEVELS' - which is how the cycle stands in for the hormone level. — strength of the relation: 0.9
span.quote: TAM administration resulted in the vaginal cytology of diestrus, a stage of the estrous cycle associated with low estrogen levels.

span.label: analgesia —operationalised-as→ tailflick response
span.note: strength of the relation: 1
span.quote: Immediately after training, analgesic responses were measured by a tailflick response.

span.label: RETRACTED (RE-GROUNDED) · estrogen —causes→ dendritic spine density
span.note: RETRACTED: RE-GROUNDED. The old span said `the density of dendritic spines`, which does not attest the endpoint `dendritic spine density` as a word. This sentence uses the paper's own compact form and states the effect: estrogen 'is reported to ENHANCE dendritic spine density and efficacy'. — strength of the relation: 0.9
span.quote: Estrogen is reported to enhance dendritic spine density and efficacy in the hippocampus and the amygdala ( 24 – 30 ), brain regions previously implicated in stress-induced effects on learning ( 31 , 32 ).

span.label: ovarian hormones —causes→ hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.7
span.quote: Like the effects of stress on learning reported here, these sex differences in the stress response are dependent on the presence of ovarian hormones ( 55 ).

span.label: ovariectomized —operationalised-as→ ovarian hormones
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.95
span.quote: To determine whether the detrimental effect of stress on classical conditioning was dependent on the presence of ovarian hormones, we removed the ovaries and trained stressed and unstressed female rats.

span.label: classical conditioning —operationalised-as→ delay paradigm
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.95
span.quote: A delay paradigm was used in which an 85-dB, 240-ms white noise CS with a 5-ms rise/fall time overlapped and coterminated with a 0.7-mA, 80-ms periorbital shock unconditioned stimulus (US).

span.label: active avoidance —contrasted-with→ passive avoidance
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.95
span.quote: Consequently, females tend to outperform males on active avoidance tasks while performing poorly on passive avoidance tasks ( 7 – 9 , 16 , 42 ).

span.label: ANOVA
span.quote: Exposure to the stressor had diametrically opposed effects on acquisition of the CR in males vs. females [ F (1, 36) = 14.28; P < 0.001].

span.label: interaction effect
span.quote: A significant interaction between stress, sex, and paired vs. unpaired training remained evident throughout 2 days of training (600 trials) [ F (1, 36) = 5.64; P < 0.02)].

span.label: post hoc multiple comparison test
span.quote: Post-hoc analysis using a Newman–Keuls comparison test indicated that exposure to the stressor facilitated acquisition of the CR in males ( P < 0.001), whereas exposure to the same stressor impaired acquisition in females ( P < 0.001), relative to their same-sex unstressed controls (Fig. 1 ).

span.label: Cochran's Q test
span.quote: In addition, exposure to the stressor did not elicit responses to the CS on the first trial of training [Cochran Q test ( 3 ) = 0.82; P = 0.85], before any learning could have occurred.

span.label: standard deviation
span.quote: The maximum value of a 240-ms pre-CS baseline response was added to 4 times its SD, and electromyographic responses greater than that were considered eyeblinks.

span.label: p-value
span.quote: Females outperformed males under unstressed conditions ( P < 0.01).

span.label: F
span.quote: diametrically opposed effects on acquisition of the CR in males vs. females [ F (1, 36) = 14.28; P < 0.001]

span.label: Newman–Keuls comparison test
span.quote: Post-hoc analysis using a Newman–Keuls comparison test indicated that exposure to the stressor facilitated acquisition of the CR in males ( P < 0.001)

span.label: Cochran Q test
span.quote: In addition, exposure to the stressor did not elicit responses to the CS on the first trial of training [Cochran Q test ( 3 ) = 0.82; P = 0.85]

span.label: significant interaction
span.quote: A significant interaction between stress, sex, and paired vs. unpaired training remained evident throughout 2 days of training (600 trials) [ F (1, 36) = 5.64; P < 0.02)]

span.label: SD
span.quote: The maximum value of a 240-ms pre-CS baseline response was added to 4 times its SD

span.label: The same stressor had opposite effects by sex: it speeded acquisition of the conditioned eyeblink response in males and slowed it in females, each relative to its own unstressed controls.
span.quote: Post-hoc analysis using a Newman–Keuls comparison test indicated that exposure to the stressor facilitated acquisition of the CR in males ( P < 0.001), whereas exposure to the same stressor impaired acquisition in females ( P < 0.001), relative to their same-sex unstressed controls (Fig. 1 ).

span.label: Without stress, females acquired the conditioned response faster than males.
span.quote: Females outperformed males under unstressed conditions ( P < 0.01).

span.label: Removing the ovaries abolished the stress-induced impairment: stress impaired acquisition in females with intact ovaries but not in ovariectomized females.
span.quote: A post-hoc Newman–Keuls comparison test revealed that acquisition was impaired by stress in females with intact ovaries ( P < 0.01), but not in females without ovaries ( P = 0.44).

span.label: Blocking estrogen receptors with tamoxifen also abolished the impairment: stress impaired acquisition in vehicle-injected females but not in tamoxifen-injected females.
span.quote: Post-hoc analysis using a Newman–Keuls comparison test revealed that exposure to the stressor impaired acquisition in the VEH ( P < 0.05), but did not alter acquisition in females injected with the estrogen antagonist TAM ( P = 0.44).

span.label: The opposite effects of stress on the two sexes were not caused by changes in spontaneous blinking, sensitization or pseudoconditioning.
span.quote: Therefore, the sexually opposed effects of stress on acquisition of the CR was not attributable to nonspecific effects of stressor exposure on spontaneous blinking, sensitization, or pseudoconditioning.

span.label: Lowering the CS intensity so that unstressed females started at a male-like acquisition rate did not remove the impairment, ruling out a ceiling effect as its cause.
span.quote: After stressor exposure, however, females were still significantly impaired relative to the unstressed females [ F (1, 16) = 10.33; P < 0.005] (Fig. 4 ).

span.label: Stressed males and stressed females did not differ in pain sensitivity as measured by tailflick latency, so the sex-opposite learning effects were not caused by differences in analgesia.
span.quote: stressed males and stressed females did not differ in their tailflick response to a painful photobeam of increasing intensity [ F (1, 40) = 0.35; P = 0.55] (Fig. 3 ).

span.label: Late in training, stressed ovariectomized females actually responded more than unstressed ovariectomized females, that is, they showed the male-like facilitation once ovarian hormones were gone.
span.quote: In fact, during the last 100 trials, OVX females exposed to the stressor responded more than the unstressed OVX females [ F (2, 68) = 3.34; P = 0.04], suggesting that the performance of OVX females can be facilitated in response to the stressor

span.label: Ovariectomy on its own impaired learning in unstressed females during the later part of acquisition.
span.quote: The loss of ovarian hormones also resulted in a learning impairment among unstressed females during late acquisition (last 100 out of 300 trials).

span.label: The unstressed female advantage disappeared with continued training, whereas the stress effect persisted, showing the two differences have different durabilities.
span.quote: During the last 100 trials, unstressed males were performing at a similar rate as unstressed females ( P = 0.26).

span.label: the same stressor had opposite effects by sex — facilitating acquisition in males and impairing it in females
span.quote: Exposure to the stressor had diametrically opposed effects on acquisition of the CR in males vs. females [ F (1, 36) = 14.28; P < 0.001]

span.label: unstressed females outperformed unstressed males
span.quote: Females outperformed males under unstressed conditions ( P < 0.01).

span.label: the baseline sex difference disappeared by the last 100 trials while the stress effect persisted across 600 trials
span.quote: During the last 100 trials, unstressed males were performing at a similar rate as unstressed females ( P = 0.26).

span.label: lowering the CS to 80 dB brought unstressed females down to the male starting rate and the stress impairment remained, so it is not a ceiling effect
span.quote: After stressor exposure, however, females were still significantly impaired relative to the unstressed females [ F (1, 16) = 10.33; P < 0.005]

span.label: ovariectomy prevented the stress-induced impairment; sham surgery did not
span.quote: A post-hoc Newman–Keuls comparison test revealed that acquisition was impaired by stress in females with intact ovaries ( P < 0.01), but not in females without ovaries ( P = 0.44).

span.label: ovariectomised females went the other way late in training, responding more after stress — the male pattern
span.quote: In fact, during the last 100 trials, OVX females exposed to the stressor responded more than the unstressed OVX females [ F (2, 68) = 3.34; P = 0.04]

span.label: blocking estrogen receptors with tamoxifen prevented the stress-induced impairment, while the injections alone had no effect on acquisition
span.quote: Post-hoc analysis using a Newman–Keuls comparison test revealed that exposure to the stressor impaired acquisition in the VEH ( P < 0.05), but did not alter acquisition in females injected with the estrogen antagonist TAM ( P = 0.44). The series of TAM or VEH injections, however, had no effect on acquisition alone ( P = 0.77).

span.label: removing the ovaries impaired learning in unstressed females late in training, so ovarian hormones also carry the baseline female advantage
span.quote: In contrast, removal of circulating ovarian hormones impaired performance during the last 100 trials of training ( P < 0.05).

span.label: no sex difference in spontaneous blink rate, in responses to the tone before training, or to explicitly unpaired stimuli
span.quote: There were no sex differences in spontaneous blink rate prior to stressor exposure [ F (1, 40) = 0.00; P = 1.0], eyeblink responses to the auditory stimulus prior to paired training [ F (1, 40) = 1.14; P = 0.29] or responses to explicitly unpaired stimulus presentations [ F (1, 12) = 0.22; P = 0.65]

span.label: stressed males and stressed females did not differ in tailflick analgesia, so the effect is not a pain-sensitivity difference
span.quote: Despite previous reports of sex differences in analgesic responses ( 36 ), stressed males and stressed females did not differ in their tailflick response to a painful photobeam of increasing intensity [ F (1, 40) = 0.35; P = 0.55]

span.label: unstressed females reached 72% responding in the first 20 trials against 37% for unstressed males
span.quote: Acquisition during the first 20 trials was significantly higher in unstressed females (72% ± 11) than in unstressed males (37% ± 8%).

span.label: tamoxifen produced a diestrus cytology in 20 of 21 females, confirming the intended low-estrogen state
span.quote: The vaginal smears of females administered TAM (20 of 21) contained leukocytes and scattered epithelial cells, a cytology indicative of diestrus and low levels of estrogen.

span.label: ovariectomy alone roughly doubled sensitized responding, from under 1 in 10 to 2 in 10
span.quote: Ovariectomy alone enhanced the number of sensitized responses from <1 of 10, to 2 of 10 responses to a white noise stimulus alone [ F (1, 34) = 5.96; P < 0.05].

span.label: the stressor did not produce responses to the tone on the very first trial, before learning was possible
span.quote: In addition, exposure to the stressor did not elicit responses to the CS on the first trial of training [Cochran Q test ( 3 ) = 0.82; P = 0.85], before any learning could have occurred.

span.label: learned helplessness
